name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
license: Proprietary API for now (MiniMax says model weights will be released later)
archDisplay: architecture undisclosed (MiniMax cites 'more aggressive sparsity' than M3; no model card or weights yet); 1M-token context, text/image/video input, always-on thinking with effort low to max
note: MiniMax's Oct 19, 2026 general release of the Flash model it had tested as M3.1-Flash-Preview inside MiniMax Code since Sep 27 (and anonymously as 'Space Bunny' on OpenRouter). Served on the MiniMax API, M Plan and MiniMax Code at a flat $0.15/$0.60 per Mtok ($0.015 cached input); MiniMax says agentic-task cost is 70% below M3 and output speed is about 3x faster. Thinking cannot be turned off and defaults to max effort. Weights are promised later, so openness stays closed until they land. NOT FILED: the launch comparison table is an image, and only the figures MiniMax also states in the post's text are filed (DeepSWE, OSWorld 2.0, CyberGym). Terminal-Bench 4.0 38.1, NL2Repo 61.2, HLE 43.4 and Automation-Bench 62.8 appear only in that image and in secondary mirrors (which disagree on Automation-Bench: 62.8 vs 62.2). Agents' Last Exam 29.6 is a pass rate (the same table gives GPT-5.6 Sol 30.6, against its 52.7 score component), so it is not filed under the corpus's score-component convention. BankerToolBench (76.2), LOCA-Bench, PostTrainBench, SWE Refactor Bench and GDP.pdf AA have no corpus column; AutomationBench-AA is Artificial Analysis's variant, not the Zapier column.
